<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**8** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **215** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **155** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **155**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **100** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **13** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a08e059c61f6ea4784d400c40ddedd3c81495bef` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `3a266c7e739752a9d4b2d04b9fe0c918ab8af37c` — the merge of head `89e02a2521f36984272b9b2401822c88f71ad0e5` into base `a08e059c61f6ea4784d400c40ddedd3c81495bef`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 3a266c7e739752a9d4b2d04b9fe0c918ab8af37c && git checkout 3a266c7e739752a9d4b2d04b9fe0c918ab8af37c
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin a08e059c61f6ea4784d400c40ddedd3c81495bef 89e02a2521f36984272b9b2401822c88f71ad0e5 && git checkout -B drift-repro a08e059c61f6ea4784d400c40ddedd3c81495bef && git merge --no-ff 89e02a2521f36984272b9b2401822c88f71ad0e5

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json a08e059c61f6ea4784d400c40ddedd3c81495bef
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `89e02a2521f36984272b9b2401822c88f71ad0e5`

Scope: 8 files (+1004/−12) on merge base `fe677aeeed`:
- `.changeset/20024-like-stored-nul.md` (new);
- one-bullet corrections of `.changeset/20024-sqlite-glob-stored-nul.md` and `.changeset/20041-like-nul-pattern-refused.md`;
- `sql-driver.ts`: the `likePatternPredicate` SQLite arm, plus the private `sqliteLikePatternPlan` / `sqliteLikePatternMatch`;
- `remote-transport.ts`: `pushLikePattern` only;
- three new pin suites.

Compile surfaces:
- face 1 TOUCHED (`SqliteWasmDriver` and local `TursoDriver` inherit it);
- face 2 TOUCHED (`RemoteTransport.pushLikePattern`);
- faces 3 and 4 not touched: `$like` / `$ilike` are in analytics' unevaluated set;
- face 5 (`formula`) is the oracle;
- `having-filter.ts` has no `$like`;
- `driver-memory` was measured;
- `driver-mongodb` and the Postgres / MySQL arms are NOT MEASURED.

Measured in detached worktrees at head and base, with the reviewer's own builds, grid and probes.

### ① Derived judgments

- **Exactness, on the reviewer's OWN grid:** 135 stored values × 242 queries per face.
  - The values include U+0000 in every position, doubled and tripled, beside multibyte, CJK, U+0001–U+0003, U+0080 and U+0100, the stand-in candidates alone and inside words, characters outside the BMP, and NULL.
  - The queries include `\%`, `\_` and `\\`, `_` over multibyte, `''`, `%` and `%%`, GLOB metacharacters as literals, patterns naming every candidate below U+0080 and U+0100, `$ilike` with ASCII and non-ASCII letters, and 23 `$not` / `$or` / `$and` compositions.
  - The four faces: better-sqlite3 3.53.4, sql.js 3.49.1, local `TursoDriver`, and remote `TursoDriver` over a real `@libsql/client` 3.45.1.
  - **Head, identical on all four faces:** 0 of 15488 BMP cells with U+0000 differ from `formula`. NUL-free BMP cells: 0 of 14278. NULL: 0 of 242. Refusals: 0. `driver-memory` differs in 0 cells anywhere.
  - **Base:** 831 of 15488 BMP cells with U+0000 differ, and 174 of 242 queries are wrong on at least one U+0000 row. The changeset's examples reproduce.
  - The only cells still differing are the pre-existing `_` divergence for characters outside the BMP. Each one equals the code-point oracle, and none is unexplained.
- **Attempts to break the stand-in argument all held:**
  - escaped literals (`\`+U+0001, `\%`, `\_`, `\\`) enter the literal set;
  - case fold: the stand-in is spliced in after `lower()`, so it can never be folded;
  - values holding both the chosen stand-in and U+0000;
  - patterns naming every candidate below U+0080 and below U+0100, which forces a 2-byte stand-in;
  - a stand-in forced onto `*`, `?`, `[` or `\`;
  - 1000 and 2000 consecutive U+0000s against `_`×1000 / ×2000;
  - two CTEs in one `$and`.

  `likePatternToGlobPattern` emits only `*`, `?` and self-closing `[x]` classes, so no literal position can match the stand-in.
- **Control:** 0 of 15972 NUL-free and NULL cells moved from base to head on every face. There are 0 new refusals. A pattern holding U+0000, and a dangling escape, still refuse `INVALID_FILTER` / 400.
- **Plans (`EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN`, identical on all three engines):**
  - `$like 'ab%'`, `'%'`, `'%%'` and `$ilike 'ab%'` keep the base statement and bindings.
  - The other patterns with a literal prefix keep `SEARCH … USING COVERING INDEX (v>? AND v<?)`, plus a correlated scalar subquery.
  - Patterns that scanned before still scan. No index SEARCH is lost.
- **Cost, the reviewer's own reading** (10k rows, median of 7):
  - 0% of rows holding U+0000: 1.25–1.91× (`'ab%'` 1.00×), head max 4.07 ms;
  - 10%: 2–5×;
  - 100%: up to 35× (≤ 32 ms).

  The direction and the absolute head times agree with the dev's table, and every head count equals the oracle's.
- **Remote parity, executed:** over 16 patterns, the statement captured from a real libSQL client carries the local predicate text (modulo quoting) and equal bindings. It runs on libSQL, and literal-prefix patterns keep their index. The grid on the remote face reads 0 of 15488.
- **The pins discriminate.** The three ablations re-ran to the dev's exact counts, then were restored by blob:
  - dispatch reverted: 25/40, 15/7, 16/7;
  - stand-in fixed at U+0001: 4/61, 2/20, 2/21;
  - remote emitter only: turso 17/6.
- **Public surface and accept set:** both new helpers are module-private (absent from every package entry and from the built export keys). Nothing that was accepted is refused.
- **Changeset `20024-like-stored-nul.md` and the PR body:** no FALSE sentence. The dev's grid counts (359/3380, 16640) come from an uncommitted probe and were not reproduced to the cell; their direction, and every reading that could be reproduced, were confirmed. The body's "base counts differ wherever U+0000 rows exist" can fail by cancellation (two 10% cells).
- **Merge with current `main`:** `git merge-tree` against `a08e059c61` is clean. Draft PR #20104's `remote-transport.ts` hunks (`:1798`, `:2659`) are disjoint from this PR's `pushLikePattern` hunks, and merge-tree of the two heads is clean too.
- **CI at this head:** 41 runs: 34 `success`, 5 `skipped`, 2 `failure`, 0 pending. Every required context is `success`. Both failures are `Check Changeset`: `check-empty-changeset` refuses the `M` rows on the two corrected changesets. That is the expected red.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` for `driver-sql`, `driver-sqlite-wasm` and `driver-turso`, with `Clause-②: no` and no direction arm: RIGHT. There is no new export and no added refusal, and a wrong answer set is corrected toward the spec's `likePatternToRegexSource`. This agrees with landing record 5823785768.
- `check-changeset-no-major --event <PR body>`: "✓ This diff introduces no `major` bump." and "✓ LEVEL AXIS: this PR declares clause-② `no` …" (exit 0).
- `check-adr-0087-registration`: "✓ … this PR adds no declared-breaking changeset (3 non-breaking changeset(s) seen)." (exit 0).
- `check-empty-changeset`: exit 1 by design, naming both corrected files.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **DELIBERATE CORRECTION confirmed on `89e02a2521`: `.changeset/20024-sqlite-glob-stored-nul.md`,** line 29 of 29 only.
  - The base bullet ("`$like` and `$ilike` still compile to `GLOB` on SQLite, so they still read a stored value only up to its first U+0000 …") is FALSE at head.
  - The head bullet ("`$like` and `$ilike` are outside this entry. Two other entries in this release cover them: on SQLite they now read the whole stored value as well, and every driver that answers `$like` refuses a pattern holding U+0000 …") is TRUE at head.
- **DELIBERATE CORRECTION confirmed on `89e02a2521`: `.changeset/20041-like-nul-pattern-refused.md`,** line 36 of 44 only. This was ruled onto this PR by amendment 5830697185.
  - The base bullet ("… still differs from `formula` on the SQLite faces … No refusal of the pattern can reach that half.") is FALSE at head.
  - The head bullet ("… is not refused: it is well formed, and on the SQLite faces it reads the whole stored value, by its own entry in this release.") is TRUE at head.
- #20041's line 32 ("every `$like` / `$ilike` pattern without U+0000 answers exactly as before") is TRUE in its scope. The corrected line 36 qualifies it in the same entry.
- **The dev's deviations are accepted:**
  - there is no shared compiler, because that would need a new `driver-sql` export; the `pushLike` precedent is followed, and the parity pin discriminates;
  - there is no prefix conjunct for `$ilike`, because `lower(col)` has no index range;
  - the turso grid is held to the spec's `matchesLikePattern`, which `formula` delegates to.
- **The dev's out-of-scope finding, `_` for characters outside the BMP (pre-existing):** REAL, and reachable at a public door, measured at head. This PR does not widen it: those cells are identical at base and head. Filing is the seat's call.
- **The per-row cost is disclosed in the changeset:** the `instr(CAST(v AS BLOB), X'00')` guard costs 1.25–1.9× on data without U+0000.
- **NOT MEASURED, declared:** the Postgres and MySQL arms (untouched), a real Turso server's wire encoding of U+0000, and `driver-mongodb`.

Implemented-by: `claude/issue-20024-like-stored-nul`
Reviewed-by: `session_01Bvd69VPa6puiNzzPUroDBx`

**VERDICT: PASS**
